key_insight: A noise-aware emulator can quantitatively predict neutral-atom analog quantum processor behavior by propagating dominant hardware imperfections through the full computation cycle.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical validation tool for Pasqal-style Rydberg atom devices, helping engineers identify dominant error sources and improve algorithm design and hardware performance.
method: Model dominant noise mechanisms across the full analog quantum workflow
Benchmark the emulator on quantum annealing and post-quench dynamics
Compare predictions against classical ground truth on three processors
evidence_signal: Across three Pasqal devices, the measured observables stayed within the emulator’s predicted uncertainty envelopes for both benchmark protocols.
watch_item: Validation is demonstrated in regimes where classical simulation is still feasible, so extension to truly classically intractable settings remains to be proven.
paper_title: Noise-aware emulation and cross-device validation of neutral atom analog quantum processing units
